messages.author: ab8dbe3bec292afe
messages.subject: Re: CIM?
parts:
Dear Alan,

One can do composite interval mapping in R/qtl. If you have complete
genotype data at a marker, it can be included as an additive covariate
in scanone() or scantwo().

However, I don't particularly like the automated procedures for CIM
(such as using forward selection to a fixed number of markers), and so
I've not implemented such procedures. I expect to do this eventually,
but I have a long list of other things that I view as more important.

karl
